title: Aloha shirt
blurb: The short-sleeved Hawaiian shirt printed with palms, flowers and surf, made for holidays and good moods.

title: Aran jumper
blurb: A thick cream wool sweater from Ireland's Aran Islands, covered in cable stitches said to bring fishermen luck.

title: Breton shirt
blurb: The navy-and-white striped top of the French navy, adopted by artists, sailors and people who summer well.

title: Duffel coat
blurb: A heavy hooded wool coat fastened with wooden toggles and rope loops, easy to do up with frozen fingers.

title: Hoodie
blurb: A sweatshirt with a hood and a kangaroo pocket: first made for cold warehouse workers, now the uniform of comfort.

title: Kimono
blurb: Japan's T-shaped wrapped robe, tied with an obi sash and often carrying seasonal patterns.

title: Leather jacket
blurb: From aviators to rock bands, the leather jacket has spent a century making its wearer look ready for trouble.

title: Levi's 501
blurb: The button-fly blue jean patented in the 1870s for miners, and the template for almost every pair of jeans since.

title: Little black dress
blurb: A simple black evening dress, popularised in the 1920s, designed to be right for nearly any occasion.

title: Poncho
blurb: A single sheet of woven cloth with a hole for the head, an Andean answer to wind and cold.

title: Sari
blurb: An unstitched length of cloth, up to nine yards long, draped in dozens of regional styles across South Asia.

title: Trench coat
blurb: A belted, double-breasted raincoat born in the First World War and worn ever since by detectives, editors and anyone caught in drizzle.

title: Tuxedo
blurb: The black-tie dinner suit with satin lapels, for evenings that call for a little ceremony.
